note_en: Chinese often marks a condition with 的 at the end of a clause, a formal legal pattern: 子女已满八周岁的，法院……应当尊重其真实意愿 "where the child has reached eight, the court must respect the child's wishes." English needs "if" or "where" at the front; Chinese tacks 的 on at the end. Watch for the bookish pronoun 其 "his/her/its" as well (其真实意愿 "the child's genuine wishes").
